meta.title: Sources
meta.description: The legal and regulatory documents every answer is built from, and when each was last checked.

heading: What this is built on
standfirst: Every answer comes from these sources. Here is what is in them, where they came from, and when they were last checked.

verified.heading: Official sources answers are built from
verified.standfirst: Ask Sahayak answers from these {{count}} official documents and portals. Each was checked against its official page on {{date}}, and every answer links back to the one it relied on — open it to read the provision yourself.

notFetched.title: Full-text library in preparation
notFetched.body: The library below is the wider set of instruments being prepared for full-text search. Until a document is indexed, answers come from the verified sources above; where one of them already covers a document below, its official link is shown.

corpus.heading: Full-text library
corpus.layer: The wider set of instruments being prepared for full-text search. Where a verified source above already covers one, its official link is shown here.

groups.indian_drug_food_cosmetic: Indian drug, food and cosmetic regulation
groups.biodiversity_abs: Biodiversity and access and benefit sharing

records.heading: Registry and records data
records.layer: Layer 2 — evidential. These are never cited as authority.
records.standingNote: These are records of what has been filed, granted or registered. They are not statements of law. They never enter the search index, they never appear as a citation, and they never raise or lower an answer's confidence. Where an answer shows related records, it shows them beside the answer and labelled, not inside it.

access.portal_link_only: Interactive portal — linked out to, never fetched

records.portalNote: Search this on the official portal. This site links to it rather than searching on your behalf.

honest.heading: How this is kept honest
honest.standfirst: Each commitment, and how it is kept.

primary.mechanism: Answers cite primary official sources — Acts, Rules, official guidelines and government portals — never commentary.

versions.mechanism: Every document carries effective_from, supersedes and superseded_by. Superseded text is retained but excluded from retrieval for current answers.

dates.mechanism: as_of_date and corpus_version are fields on the Answer model, shown on every response.

beyond.mechanism: Generation is constrained to the retrieved passages, and an answer the passages do not support returns an abstention instead.

uncertainty.mechanism: Confidence is computed from the retrieval result and always shown with a one-sentence reason.

check.mechanism: Every citation carries its document, section path and link, and the retrieved passage can be opened in the words it was published in.

subscription.mechanism: Never scraped. Accessed only through the reader's own credentials, with per-session consent, and every access logged and shown back to them.

escalate.mechanism: Every answer carries a route to a qualified facilitator, packaging the question, jurisdiction, product class and sources into a summary.

notCovered.heading: What this does not cover
notCovered.standfirst: Stated plainly, because a product that hides its limits is asking to be trusted where it should not be.

items.clinical: No clinical or dosage advice, and no opinion on whether a preparation is safe or effective for a person.
items.drafting: No drafting of applications, specifications, responses or agreements.
items.outcome: No opinion on whether an application will be granted, refused or opposed.
items.jurisdictions: No jurisdictions beyond those listed above. A question about a country not in the source set gets no answer rather than a plausible one.
items.realtime: No real-time registry status. Records are snapshots with a date on them, and the date is shown.
items.novelty: No novelty conclusions. The prior-art tools help you search; they do not search every database an examiner would consult.
items.representation: No legal representation, and no relationship that could be mistaken for one.
